question: What is the main goal behind how an operating room is designed?

options.A: Minimizing infection risk and keeping patients safe
options.B: Allowing family members to watch procedures
options.C: Speeding up the recovery time after surgery
options.D: Reducing the cost of surgical instruments

explanation: Spot on! Everything in the operating room layout is carefully planned to keep the area sterile and protect our patients from infections. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why do we strictly control the movement of people inside a surgical suite?

options.A: To ensure the nurses finish their paperwork on time
options.B: To make sure doctors do not get lost in the hospital
options.C: To keep the surgical equipment from being stolen
options.D: To prevent the spread of microorganisms into sterile areas

explanation: Exactly! Limiting unnecessary movement means less dust and fewer germs floating around, which helps keep the surgical field super clean and safe. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is most likely done in a standard general operating theatre?
explanation: Great choice! General operating theatres are built for everyday, standard procedures like hernia repairs and appendectomies, leaving the high-tech rooms for specialized surgeries. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h2)

question: A patient is booked for an elective knee joint replacement. Which theatre is best suited for this?
explanation: You got it! Joint surgeries need special tools and special airflow systems found in orthopaedic theatres to keep deep wounds free from infection. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h2)

question: What makes a modern modular operating theatre special in terms of structure?

options.A: Seamless, pre-fabricated panels that resist bacterial growth
options.B: Wooden flooring to absorb sound and reduce echoes
options.C: Traditional painted concrete walls that are easy to repaint
options.D: Open windows to allow natural sunlight during daytime surgery

explanation: Spot on! Modular theatres use smooth, factory-made panels so there are no tiny cracks or corners where stubborn germs and dust can hide. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why do hospitals love using modular theatres with integrated digital control panels?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any nurses inside the room
options.B: To reduce the cost of electricity used by surgical lights
options.C: To allow patients to watch movies during local anesthesia
options.D: To streamline equipment controls and improve communication efficiency

explanation: Brilliant! Having gas outlets, lights, and communication tools in one central smart hub makes everything run much smoother during a busy case. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which of these procedures is typically done in a casualty or minor theatre?

options.B: Performing an open heart valve replacement

explanation: Correct! Minor procedures like stitching up cuts fit perfectly in the casualty theatre, freeing up the big ORs for massive surgeries. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the biggest advantage of having a separate casualty theatre in the hospital?

options.A: It completely removes the need for sterilization protocols
options.B: It reduces the number of doctors required on duty
options.C: It allows student nurses to perform surgeries independently
options.D: It preserves major operating theatres for complex and major surgeries

explanation: You nailed it! Separating minor cases from major ones ensures our heavy-duty ORs are always ready when a major surgical emergency rolls in. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h4)

question: Where are emergency and trauma operating suites usually placed in a hospital layout?

options.A: In a separate building far from the main wards
options.B: On the top floor near the administrative offices
options.C: Close to the emergency department for fast access
options.D: Next to the hospital laundry and kitchen facilities

explanation: Spot on! When a patient is bleeding out from a trauma, every single second counts, so being right next to the emergency department is a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h5)

question: A patient arrives from a terrible car crash with massive internal bleeding. What must the trauma suite have ready immediately?

options.A: Cosmetic laser equipment and soothing music
options.B: Long-term recovery beds for overnight stays
options.C: Rapid blood transfusion equipment and crash carts

explanation: Wonderful! Trauma suites must be stocked with rapid blood warmers and infusers to fight off hemorrhagic shock right away. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h5)

question: What clothing rule is a must when you enter the restricted zone of an operating suite?

options.A: No special clothing or personal protective gear is needed
options.B: Street clothes and ordinary shoes are allowed without restriction
options.C: Full surgical attire including masks and hair covers is mandatory
options.D: Only lab coats worn over regular clothes are required

explanation: Correct! Since this zone gets closest to the sterile field, wearing complete scrubs, caps, and masks keeps everyone safe from accidental contamination. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why do we divide an operating suite into unrestricted, semi-restricted, and restricted zones?

options.A: To progressively lower the risk of microbial contamination closer to the patient
options.B: To ensure that doctors and nurses have separate break rooms
options.C: To make it easier to clean the floors with automated machines
options.D: To prevent patients from wandering into the administrative offices

explanation: You got it! These zoning layers act like security checkpoints, filtering out dust and germs step-by-step before anyone steps near the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h6)
